feedback_rules.description: Visible errors include mistimed heel steps or loss of rhythm; arm movement variations are expressive and not errors

learning_units.description: Master rapid heel steps matching bass drum beats at 170-190 BPM
Incorporate backstep into basic hakken footwork

prerequisites.description: Ability to maintain fast foot rhythm and balance at high tempo

social_formats.description: Solo or group dancing with shared rhythm; no partnering required

movement_profile.arms_and_hands: Moved less prominently, optional and secondary to footwork
movement_profile.footwork: Rapid heel steps landing on heels in quick succession, moving forward, backward, and laterally
movement_profile.formation_and_space: Solo or group, no fixed spatial pattern
movement_profile.levels_and_jumps: No jumps described; mostly low-level footwork
movement_profile.posture: Upright with focus on lower body

signature_moves.description: A step backward incorporated into the rapid heel-driven sequence
signature_moves.name: Backstep

movement_profile.tempo_feel: Fast, steady, matching bass drum beats
movement_profile.what_to_avoid: Avoid high jumps or aerial moves not typical of hakken Avoid overemphasis on arms that distracts from foot rhythm

music_profile.rhythm_pattern: Steady, pounding bass drum on each beat
music_profile.sound_description: A relentless pounding bass drum at high tempo drives the music, with electronic synth layers and occasional vocal samples creating an intense, energetic atmosphere.

basic_steps: Repeat steps in succession matching bass drum
Add slight forward, backward, or lateral movement
teaching.formation: Solo or group, no fixed formation required
teaching.level_notes: Beginners start with heel steps matching bass drum; arms and torso movement optional and secondary
teaching.rhythm: Bass drum beat at 170-190 BPM, steady and repetitive

platform: Validated voice/movement feedback and accessible controls
Human BDF consent/matching, moderation and measured session synchronization
Tested camera/split-screen delivery; AR remains an optional future adapter
